oldBrief: This is a short regional sector. The cabin is full of young professionals on their way to meetings. The wheels of commerce keep turning thanks to your skills as a pilot.
newBrief: Coffee in hand and half-awake, the queue is long for the first flight out. Keep it smooth and get your passengers to their destination while the caffeine's still working.

oldBrief: Tonight's late commuter sector should be a quiet one. The sky is empty tonight. Climb efficiently and do not waste fuel. The company is clamping down hard and wants to save money.
newBrief: Tonight's departure board has gone quiet. Climb smoothly and don't burn fuel you don't need. Ops are watching the fuel bill with eagle eyes.

oldBrief: The clock is against you on this scheduled sector. Ask for priority on the approach, aim for vectors to finals, and get the passengers offloaded as soon as you block in.
newBrief: ATC expects you on the money today. Push for priority on the approach, line up for vectors to finals, and have the doors open the second you block in.

oldBrief: High-value, time-critical Formula One chassis needs transporting for a race. You cannot afford to make a mistake with this one. These cars cost upwards of $15 million, so take it easy.
newBrief: The team needs this chassis trackside for the weekend, and it's worth more than most people's houses. These cars run $15 million a piece, so one rough patch of air could end a season early.

oldBrief: The patient is stable, but rough air will not help their condition. Watch the weather radar and keep the ride smooth all the way in. The medical team are already on board and expecting the patient soon.
newBrief: Turbulence won't do this patient any favors, so watch the radar and keep it smooth all the way down. The medical team's already strapped in beside you.

oldBrief: First responders have a landing zone ready on the roadway. Get in, get the patient aboard and go — the clock is running.
newBrief: First responders already have the LZ marked on the roadway. Get in, get the patient aboard, go. Every second counts now.

oldBrief: You are Red Air today. Fly the briefed intercept vectors, test friendly radar response, acknowledge sim contacts, then proceed to destination.
newBrief: Your chance to be the bad guy today. Hold the briefed intercept vectors, test friendly radar response, log contacts, then continue to destination.

oldBrief: This VIP charter has a bar stocked for comfort and fun. Make the landing butter-smooth so the passenger arrives in a good mood and ignore any guffawing coming from the cabin.
newBrief: Tonight's {vip_type} expects the finer things. The bar's stocked and the cabin is ready for our guest. Keep the landing smooth enough that nobody in the cabin notices.

oldBrief: You will launch from {dep_field} and work lift toward {dest_field}. Read the sky — developing cumulus marks the thermals, with puffy tops and dark flat bases. Give decaying wispy cloud a wide berth. Stay VFR and arrive with height for a normal circuit.
newBrief: Launch from {dep_field} and go hunting for lift toward {dest_field}. Puffy-topped cumulus with a flat, dark base is where the thermals live, so give the wispy, decaying stuff a wide berth.

oldBrief: You are ferrying a vintage airframe to the museum. Treat her gently, stay well inside the structural limits — she is old and the museum wants her in one piece.
newBrief: She's not getting any younger, and the museum's waiting. Fly her gently, stay clear of the structural limits, and bring her home in one piece. This old airframe's earned an easy last leg.

oldBrief: EGLC has you on the noise-abatement departure today. Fly the steep-climb profile and keep it clean for the monitors below.
newBrief: London City's neighbours love the Whisperjet. Nail the steep-climb profile out of EGLC and keep the noise monitors quiet below.

oldBrief: Today's EGNS departure follows the noise-abatement profile. Fly the steep climb and keep it clean for the community underneath.
newBrief: EGNS keeps a tight lid on noise near the coast. Hold the steep-climb profile out and keep it quiet for the people below.

oldBrief: The Ponte Aérea run leaves SBRJ today. Use max thrust, expect a tight climbing turn right after rotation and watch the terrain closely.
newBrief: SBRJ's short runway leaves no room for hesitation. Push max thrust, hold the tight climbing turn right after rotation, and keep those terrain contours in sight the whole way up.

oldBrief: This cross-country rally will push the Comanche hard. Watch the cylinder-head temps and manage the mixture so you do not cook the engine on the trip.
newBrief: The Comanche's entered for today's cross-country rally, and she loves being pushed. Watch the cylinder-head temps, dial in the mixture, and let her stretch her legs.

oldBrief: You have pressurization and climb rate to work with today. Use both to get above the regional weather and keep your block time tight.
newBrief: You're above the weather today, not fighting through it. Climb to altitude, hold the block times, and don't forget to turn on the Oxygen for your passengers.

oldBrief: You were picked for this run because you are flying the 'Whisperjet'. Stick to the descent profile and be sure to lower flaps and gear in time for a clean landing.
newBrief: This airframe is renowned for its exceptionally low noise levels and is why you got the call today. Fly the descent profile precisely, and lower flaps and gear in time for a clean landing.

oldBrief: A local university wants optical data on changing topography below. Hold a steady low track and watch those radial engine temps on the Albatross.
newBrief: A university team wants to measure how the ground's shifted since last season. Hold a steady low track and keep an eye on the radial temps, this old Albatross runs warm.

oldBrief: Bulk provisions are bound for a distant outpost today. The Albatross is heavy and the equipment is getting old. Fly a standard approach and expect firm control inputs.
newBrief: This outpost hasn't had a resupply in weeks, and the Albatross is hauling every pound of it today. Lean on that heavy lift capacity and rugged gear. Fly a smooth approach, and expect the heavy controls this old airframe is known for.

oldBrief: Today's Albatross patrol needs eyes outside the cockpit. Stay in visual contact with the terrain where you can and fly smooth turns.
newBrief: Another quiet patrol lap for the Albatross today. Keep your eyes outside, stay tight to the terrain where you can, and grease the turns nice and smooth.

oldBrief: Today you are flying a research team to their destination. Their equipment is sensitive to being thrown around, so fly a gentle landing and no steep turns.
newBrief: The research team's gear in the back doesn't like being thrown around. Fly a gentle landing, skip the steep turns, and get this crew down on the ground.

oldBrief: The team at your destination is waiting on bulk provisions. Fly a controlled approach and check landing conditions before you arrive.
newBrief: The camp at your destination is down to its last supplies and is waiting on you. Fly a controlled approach, check the strip conditions before committing, and get the drop in clean.

oldBrief: This commemorative route honours the crews who operated these flying boats. Keep your eyes outside, stay low where you can and fly smooth, sweeping turns.
newBrief: Today's flight honours the old flying-boat crews who ran search and rescue in the Albatross. Keep your eyes outside and stay low where the terrain allows.

oldBrief: {team}, the coaching staff and their medical kit are aboard. Keep the climb and descent gentle so nobody is bouncing around before the whistle blows.
newBrief: {team}, the coaching staff and the medical team are en route to their next match. Keep the climb and descent gentle so nobody's out of their seat before the whistle blows.

oldBrief: The cabin is full of holiday passengers on annual leave. Give them a steady ride and let their holidays start early.
newBrief: This cabin's buzzing with excitement all around. It looks like a lot of your passengers have already started the party before boarding the aircraft. Uh-oh.

oldBrief: Yesterday's storms grounded half the network. You have a full cabin of tired passengers who just need to get where they were meant to be.
newBrief: Yesterday's storms took out half the network and these people been waiting it out. Get your passengers to where they were meant to be, steady and on time.

oldBrief: This is a scheduled hub link: heavy metal and big airports. Fly the filed route and settle her early on the approach.
newBrief: Heavy metal, big airports, no surprises expected today. Fly the filed route and settle her in early on the approach.

oldBrief: The cabin is packed with tourists in holiday mood, and the schedule is relentless. Hit the block times or you will hear about it at the gate.
newBrief: This cabin's bursting with excited holidaymakers but the schedule isn't slowing down for anyone. Hit the block times or you'll hear about it at the gate.

oldBrief: Tech professionals will have their laptops open from pushback. Keep the cruise smooth so they can get their work done on time.
newBrief: Laptops are open before the door's even shut. Keep the cruise smooth so this crowd gets their work done before wheels down.

oldBrief: The sky is busy on this peak-season holiday route. Listen for holds, watch the fuel and do not get caught short if ATC stacks you up.
newBrief: Peak season means a full sky and zero patience for delay. Listen for holds, watch the fuel, and don't get caught short if ATC stacks you up.

oldBrief: The passengers have been stuck for hours after the network went down. Climb smoothly, plan ahead during Cruise and call for Top of descent early. Time to get these people back home.
newBrief: The network's been down for hours and these passengers are exhausted. Climb smooth, plan ahead, call for top of descent early, and get these people home.

oldBrief: A corporate group is in the back after a long week away at a global offsite. No need for chatty PAs tonight. Fly a quiet, smooth sector and bring these folks back home.
newBrief: This corporate group's had a long week away at their global offsite. Fly the route, no deviations from the plan and get these people home.

oldBrief: Today's sector is the airline's flagship route. Fly quickly and safely and expect a quick turnaround once the passengers have disembarked and you have refuelled.
newBrief: This is the airline's flagship sector, so fly it well. Expect a fast turnaround the moment the tanks are full again.

oldBrief: Ordinary line flying is on the board today. Fly it by the book and keep to the schedule. This is what you trained for. You are in charge of a $350 million aircraft, enjoy the flight.
newBrief: Ordinary line flying, nothing more. Fly it by the book, keep to the schedule, and remember you're in charge of a $350 million aircraft. Enjoy it.

oldBrief: You are shuttling morning business passengers between hubs. ATC has a full sky today, so hold the assigned speed and plan ahead. Call for top of descent and who knows, you might even get vectored to the top of the glideslope if you're lucky.
newBrief: Morning business traffic between hubs, and a full sky to match. Hold the assigned speed, plan ahead, and call for top of descent. You might even get vectored all the way to the IAF if you're lucky.

oldBrief: University students have taken over your cabin on their way to a massive event. Expect lots of overhead cabins opening and closing and, if it gets rowdy back there, send in the cavalry and turn the seat belt signs on.
newBrief: University students have taken over the cabin on the way to a massive event. Expect dancing in the aisles, and if it gets rowdy back there, the seatbelt sign is your best friend.

oldBrief: A touring symphony orchestra need to get to their next concert. You now have a hold full of instrument cases that do not bounce well. Fly a clean departure and watch the weather radar for turbulence.
newBrief: A touring symphony orchestra needs to make their next concert, and the hold's full of instrument cases that do not bounce well. Plan ahead and keep an eye on the radar for turbulence.

oldBrief: A cabin of excited exchange students is headed to their host families. Nothing fancy is needed today, just a safe, smooth flight and no delays.
newBrief: A cabin full of excited exchange students headed to their host families. Nothing fancy needed today, just a safe, smooth flight and no delays.

oldBrief: Company personnel are headed to a major post-merger integration seminar. The cabin is full and it's up to you to get the workforce to their destination on time and in one piece.
newBrief: Company personnel are headed to a major post-merger seminar, and the cabin's full to capacity today.

oldBrief: You have a lively team of sports fans filling the cabin today. Warn the crew to steel themselves as some fans are already celebrating in row twelve.
newBrief: A lively crowd of fans is filling this cabin on their way to the final. Give the cabin crew a heads-up, row twelve's already celebrating.

oldBrief: Retired sun-seekers fill every seat. Give them a soft rotation, a soft landing and don't spill their Bloody Marys with steep turns.
newBrief: Every row is full of retirees chasing warmer skies for the winter. Give them a soft landing and don't spill their Bloody Marys with steep turns.

oldBrief: A string of short sectors is on today's roster. Keep the cabin cool on the ground, use Hotel mode if your airframe has it and stay clear of developing weather fronts.
newBrief: Today's roster is a string of short sectors back to back. Keep the cabin cool between hops, flip on Hotel mode if you've got it, and steer clear of any weather building nearby.

oldBrief: This run matters to the towns it serves. Stick to the schedule as plenty of passengers are counting on a connection at the other end.
newBrief: This run matters more than it looks. Stick to the schedule, there's a whole community counting on you making the connection at the other end.

oldBrief: You have a full cabin of tired short-haul passengers who just want to get back home after yesterday's groundings.
newBrief: Yesterday's groundings left a cabin full of tired short-haul passengers who just want to be home. Get them there.

oldBrief: Every seat is taken on this regional sector. Hit the block times and tell the crew that the passengers are ready to start their holiday when the doors open.
newBrief: Every seat's taken and everyone's ready for the doors to open so that they can start their holiday. Hit the block times and let the crew know it's go the second we're on stand.

oldBrief: The network system has been down for hours. You have a full cabin of tired passengers who need to get home. Fly a clean descent and keep your passengers happy by keeping the chatter to a minimum.
newBrief: The system's been down for hours and the passengers are worn out. Fly a clean descent and keep the chatter low, they've had enough noise for one day.

oldBrief: Today you are flying a corporate group to an international tradeshow. Your passengers are excited to get to their destination and start networking or is that not working.
newBrief: This corporate group's headed to an international tradeshow, buzzing to get in the door and start networking. Or is that not working, we'll let them find out.

oldBrief: This is the busiest regional feeder in the network. Get the passengers on, fly the route, get to the gate, turnaround and repeat. You have a busy day ahead of you captain.
newBrief: This is the busiest feeder in the network today. Load them up, fly the route, get to the gate, turn it around and do it again. Busy day, captain.

oldBrief: You have ordinary hub feeder route today. Ask ATC nicely for any shortcuts they can give you, so you can shut down and get out of the airport to that party you were invited to. Time off work is a wonderful thing.
newBrief: Nothing special about today's hub feeder, it's just the daily grind. Ask ATC nicely for a shortcut if they've got one, it might get you to that party on time. Time off is a wonderful thing.

oldBrief: Excited exchange students are on their way to their host families. Keep it smooth, keep it punctual and no dad jokes please.
newBrief: Excited exchange students are headed to their host families tonight. Keep it smooth, keep it punctual, and let's skip the dad jokes this leg.

oldBrief: Company staff need transporting to a seminar after a recent merger. It is a full-cabin and a short sector. Let's hope everyone gets to keep their jobs this time.
newBrief: Staff are headed to a seminar after the merger, short sector, full cabin. Here's hoping everyone still has a desk to come back to.

oldBrief: {name} wants the cabin quiet the whole way. Fly a smooth climb, a smooth descent and don't spill the champagne with steep turns.
newBrief: {name} wants a quiet cabin tonight, nothing but the soothing hum of the engines. Keep the climb soft, the descent softer, and mind the turns, you don't want our guests spilling their champagne all over the seats.

oldBrief: {athlete} is on board, and you have been booked to fly them to their next event. Fly smoothly so {athlete} can rest during the flight.
newBrief: {athlete} needs a quiet cabin to rest and relax in. Keep it smooth end to end so they land rested, not rattled.

oldBrief: Executives are working a deal in the back. Give them a soft ride and no drama on the way to the negotiation. If you're feeling naughty, you could use FLC during climb.
newBrief: The team's working the numbers in back, no interruptions unless absolutely necessary. Keep it smooth and quiet, and if you're feeling bold, use FLC in the climb but be prepared for crazy climb rates.

oldBrief: Your cabin is an office today. The laptops are out and the chatter is constant. Keep the coffee running and fly a smooth descent.
newBrief: Today's cabin doubles as the boardroom, laptops open and non-stop chatter. Keep the coffee coming and grease that descent.

oldBrief: State representatives are on the manifest today. Fly by the book and keep it professional. You are a professional, aren't you?
newBrief: State reps are on today's manifest, press teams as well. Fly it by the book, no shortcuts. You are a professional, after all, aren't you?

oldBrief: A {vip_type} is aboard bound for a high-level conference. Keep the control inputs gentle and the cabin environment comfortable. And don't forget the red carpet!
newBrief: {vip_type} is riding to a high-level conference today. I need steady hands on the controls, a comfortable cabin, and don't you dare forget the red carpet.

oldBrief: You have executives with a tight ground schedule waiting to board. Get them to their destination early if you can. These people keep our company in the air, so treat them well.
newBrief: This executive group is getting impatient waiting in the terminal for you to choose the contract.

oldBrief: A premium share owner used to the best is aboard today's flight. Make the whole piloting thing look effortless and go as fast as you can, I heard they like big numbers.
newBrief: A fractional owner used to first-class everything is in the back today. Make it look effortless, and push the speed.

oldBrief: Prospective investors are being sold a company inside your cabin today. Keep the flight butter-smooth and keep the champagne on ice. This one is important to our client.
newBrief: The deal is being pitched in the cabin and the investors need to walk away sold on this one. Butter-smooth ride, champagne on ice, this one matters to the client.

oldBrief: Local forces need a state witness transported. Fly A to B, no fuss and don't attract attention. Park at the FBO after landing and stay away from the main terminal.
newBrief: A state witness needs moving quietly today. Fly straight to the destination, no fuss, no attention. Make sure the door is locked.

oldBrief: A Renaissance masterpiece worth more than the jet is secured to one of the seats in the cabin, which is rather strange. Keep cabin temperature chilled, and stay clear of convective weather. The world needs more art and today you are the messenger.
newBrief: A Renaissance piece worth more than the aircraft is strapped to a seat in the cabin. Keep the cabin cool, steer clear of any building weather.

oldBrief: A PR mess is brewing and the legal team need to work on their case during today's flight. Shorten the route wherever you can and bring these legal professionals to their destination.
newBrief: A PR mess is boiling over and the legal team's working the case in the back the whole way. Trim the route where you can and get counsel to the door fast.

oldBrief: A tech billionaire's fabulous feline has claimed the cabin. Keep the fish flowing, the banks shallow and the landing soft. This passenger expects the very best service on her way home.
newBrief: A tech mogul's cat has claimed the whole cabin today. Keep the fish coming, the banks shallow and the landing soft, she expects nothing less than the best.

oldBrief: {musician} wants to go shopping. Keep the champagne in the glass and turn a blind eye to any shenanigans above the clouds. What happens in the cabin, stays in the cabin. Remember that if you want to keep your job.
newBrief: {musician} is off on a shopping spree. Keep the champagne flowing and turn a blind eye to whatever's happening back there.

oldBrief: The owner of this aircraft is loading their golf clubs in the back and has asked especially for you as their pilot. It must be your sparkling personality. Enjoy the scenic approach and keep the landing soft.
newBrief: The caddy is loading the golf clubs in the back and you were hand-picked for this flight. Must be your sparkling personality. Enjoy the scenic approach and keep that landing soft.

oldBrief: Today's passengers are skipping the airline queues. Ask for directs where ATC allows and shorten your block time where you can.
newBrief: Today's passengers are dodging the airline queues. Ask ATC for directs where you can get them to trim the block time down.

oldBrief: {musician} and their management team need sleep before the show. Climb above the weather, dodge the bumps and keep cabin pressure steady. No alcohol on today's flight by order of the management.
newBrief: {musician} and the crew need sleep before tomorrow's show. Climb above the weather, dodge the bumps and hold that cabin pressure steady.

oldBrief: {name} is meeting a spiritual guru, and the press is watching this tail number. Park somewhere quiet and keep any mention of your passenger off open channels.
newBrief: {name} is meeting a spiritual guru today and the press already have your tail number. Find a quiet corner to park and keep any mention of your passenger off open channels.

oldBrief: {athlete} needs to arrive rested and on time for the championship event. Ask for priority clearance and keep the ride smooth.
newBrief: {athlete} needs to land rested and on schedule for an upcoming event. Ask for priority clearance and keep this one smooth all the way down.

oldBrief: {name} needs a discreet ride to a film premiere. Avoid the paparazzi hanging around the apron. Keep comms to a minimum, fly a clean approach and park quickly at the FBO.
newBrief: {name} needs a quiet ride to tonight's premiere. Go straight to the private FBO, as the paparazzi are waiting at the VIP terminal.

oldBrief: {team} executives are on board for an away fixture and the media are watching. Keep it professional, you are a professional aren't you? and don't forget to smile and be polite. These people keep our company in the air!
newBrief: {team} executives are riding to today's away fixture with the media watching close. These are the people keeping the company airborne.

oldBrief: The surgical team are ready to board the aircraft, and the hospital is waiting for them to arrive. Don't waste time and bring this team to the destination as quickly as you can.
newBrief: The medical team's ready to board and the hospital's waiting on them. No time to waste, get this team there fast.

oldBrief: His stock is in free-fall and the CEO needs to get back to his offices as quickly as possible to save the day. Expedite your checklists and do not forget the fuel.
newBrief: The stock's in free-fall and this CEO needs to be back at the office before the board meeting starts without him.

oldBrief: Lifeguard priority! You are carrying essential medial tissue for a transplant. Ask ATC for priority on the way in. Helicopters go to the hospital; everyone else meets the ground crew on arrival.
newBrief: This is a Lifeguard priority run, essential tissue for a transplant is secured in the back. Ask ATC to expedite the whole way in.

oldBrief: You may be heading into an uncontrolled field for this patient pickup. Check the runway before you commit to the approach.
newBrief: The patient has been stabilised and the medevac team are waiting for you to arrive. Check the runway condition before you commit to the approach.

oldBrief: Classified diplomatic files are on board chained to someone who looks like John Cena. It can't be him, can it? Don't stop for anyone unless you want to be thrown off your own plane.
newBrief: Classified files are chained to a guy who looks exactly like John Cena. It can't be him, can it?

oldBrief: You are carrying prototype hardware that is sensitive to static and temperature. Check your environmental controls before taxi and departure. If this arrives damaged, you can look for a new job in the morning.
newBrief: This prototype hardware doesn't like static or swings in temperature. Run the environmental checks before you even think about taxiing.

oldBrief: Today we have live cargo riding in the back. No, not passengers, animals! Keep the banks shallow and go easy on the thrust unless you want to re-enact The Lion King at FL200.
newBrief: Live cargo's riding in back today. Keep the banks shallow and ease off the thrust unless you're angling for a Lion King re-enactment enroute.

oldBrief: You are transporting living plants that are sensitive to pressure and temperature. Watch the descent rate on the way in and keep the cabin temps tropical.
newBrief: These saplings are alive and picky about pressure and temperature. Fly a gentle descent rate on the way in and keep the cabin tropical.

oldBrief: Unedited production footage is in the hold, and the editing suite is waiting. It's up to you to deliver the digital masters on time. We've been told a representative from Marvel will meet you at the FBO. Please let it be Deadpool.
newBrief: Unedited footage is in the hold and the editing suite's waiting on it. Get the digital masters there on schedule.

oldBrief: Climate-controlled manuscript cases have been packed into the hold. Have ground handling ready the moment you block in, these manuscripts are irreplaceable and sensitive to temperature and moisture. Keep the cabin cool and dry.
newBrief: These manuscripts are irreplaceable and fussy about both temperature and moisture. Have ground handling ready the second you block in.

oldBrief: Another aircraft has been grounded and it waiting on this part. Shorten the route where possible and fly a smooth approach.
newBrief: Another aircraft's grounded and waiting on this part. Trim the route wherever you can and grease the approach, maintenance is counting the minutes until you arrive.

oldBrief: This temperature controlled medical cargo is headed to a regional hospital. Ask ATC for priority and keep pressurization steady.
newBrief: Temperature controlled medical cargo needs flying to the regional hospital and every minute counts. Ask ATC for priority and hold that pressurization steady.

oldBrief: {med_cargo} is in the hold. Keep cabin temperatures locked in and avoid fast climbs or descents that spike the pressure.
newBrief: {med_cargo} is riding in the hold today. Lock the cabin temperature in and skip the fast climbs or descents, pressure swings won't do it any favors.

oldBrief: A clinic needs this {med_cargo} for a procedure today. Keep the block as short as you can. There will be someone waiting to meet you when you park at the FBO.
newBrief: A clinic's waiting on this {med_cargo} for a procedure today. Keep the block as tight as you can, someone will be there to meet you the moment you park at the FBO.

oldBrief: Fresh produce from the field to the hold to the shops. Get airborne while it is still cold and dry and keep an eye on cabin temps. The cabin smells amazing today.
newBrief: Fresh produce is going straight from the field to the shops today. Whatever's back there, it smells fantastic.

oldBrief: Tonight's freight run keeps the regional network moving. Hit the slots to keep things running smoothly.
newBrief: Tonight's freight run is what keeps the regional network moving. Hit your slots and keep it rolling.

oldBrief: You have an old-school mail run tonight. Weight is tight at every stop so do not hang about, you have more drops before sunset.
newBrief: Tonight's an old-school mail run and the weight's tight at every stop. Don't linger, there's more drops before the sun's down.

oldBrief: Supplies and mail are in the hold. Recheck density altitude before committing to the departure.
newBrief: Supplies and mail are loaded and customers are waiting. Recheck your density altitude before you commit to the departure.

oldBrief: A regional supply run is on the board today. Work the landing numbers for your arrival weight and use reverse if the runway is short.
newBrief: A regional supply run's on the board today. Work your landing numbers for arrival weight, and lean on reverse if the runway's tight.

oldBrief: These {med_cargo} need to get to their destination in one piece and quickly. You have been tasked with flying these essential items to their destination. Staff from the hospital will meet you on the apron. There is no time to explain, get there now!
newBrief: These {med_cargo} need to get there in one piece and fast. Hospital staff will be waiting on the apron, no time to explain, just get there.

oldBrief: It is 4 AM, the coffee is weak and your hold is full of today's news. Get the papers to the distributors before breakfast.
newBrief: It's 4 AM, the coffee's weak, and the hold's stacked with today's news. Get the papers to the distributors before breakfast beats you there.

oldBrief: The ice is already melting on this catch. Get it to the restaurants before the dinner rush and keep the cabin cold. You don't need lobsters on the loose in the cabin (again).
newBrief: The ice on this catch is already melting. Get it to the restaurants before the dinner rush. And no, we are not doing the loose lobster thing again.

oldBrief: A wealthy client's vintage car is stuck waiting on this part. Push to save time where you can, but keep the gauges in the green.
newBrief: A wealthy client's vintage car is stuck waiting on this part. Push to save time where you safely can, but keep every gauge in the green.

oldBrief: Harvest season is underway and an essential machine is down on the field. Get these parts there as fast as you safely can.
newBrief: Harvest season's in full swing and a critical machine just went down. Get these parts there as fast as you safely can, the field's waiting.

oldBrief: Last flight before the sun goes down and it's up to you to bring the regional mail to the hub for distribution to rural areas. Fly a clean pattern and butter that landing. Who knows what condition the runway is in!
newBrief: This is the last flight before the sun goes down, and the mail's got to make the hub for onward distribution.

oldBrief: Food, fuel and mail are bound for a place with no road in. Check landing performance for your destination and watch for birds on approach.
newBrief: Food, fuel and mail are bound for a community that's counting on this delivery. Watch out for birds on approach.

oldBrief: A rural estate needs materials now and it is a short strip. Watch the crosswind on final and get the freight down cleanly.
newBrief: The client is waiting for you. Watch the crosswind on final and get this pungent smelling cargo off this plane asap.

oldBrief: The regional night express depends on its slots. Hit them so the network does not stall.
newBrief: The regional night express lives and dies by its slots. Hit every one of them or the whole network stalls behind you.

oldBrief: The sort facility is on the clock. Ask for directs if there are any delays getting in the air.
newBrief: The sort facility's on the clock tonight. Ask for directs the second you sense any delay getting airborne.

oldBrief: This red-eye clears the regional hubs. Stick to the ATC slots and keep the descent clean while the skies are quiet.
newBrief: This red-eye clears the regional hubs tonight. Stick to your ATC slots and keep the descent clean while the skies stay quiet.

oldBrief: Temp-controlled medical cargo is headed to a regional hospital, and you are the quickest link. Ask ATC for priority.
newBrief: Temperature controlled medical cargo needs to get to the regional hospital and you're the quickest link there is. Ask ATC for priority and don't get distracted.

oldBrief: {med_cargo} is going direct, skipping the hubs. The lab teams are waiting, so do not waste time on the ground.
newBrief: {med_cargo} is going direct to the lab today, no hub stops. The medical teams are waiting for this equipment, so don't waste a minute on the ground.

oldBrief: You are collecting machine parts for regional farmers today. Say the word and the teams will secure the loads in the hold. Expect a sluggish climb with so much weight on board.
newBrief: You're collecting machine parts for regional farmers today. Say the word and the ground teams will secure the loads in the hold.

oldBrief: This supply run will restock regional businesses. Work the landing numbers for your arrival weight and use reverse if the runway is short.
newBrief: This run restocks regional businesses today. Work your landing numbers for arrival weight, and lean on reverse if the runway's tight.

oldBrief: A late night red-eye for a quiet regional network. Traffic is thin; fly efficiently and keep the chain moving through the night.
newBrief: It's a late-night flight through a quiet regional network tonight. Traffic's thin, so take it easy and save some fuel.

oldBrief: Local supply chains are broken and relief pallets are on board. Ask for vectors where you can and get the supplies on the ground where they are needed most.
newBrief: Check the drop zone coordinates twice, we don't want a repeat of 'cargo pallet falls through church roof' from last month.

oldBrief: Pallets of boxed clothing bound for warehouses is in the hold. Keep it clean and dry all the way down.
newBrief: Pallets of boxed clothing are bound for the warehouses today. Keep the hold clean and dry all the way down.

oldBrief: Fragile museum pieces need to be delivered for a new exhibition. Descend with care, go easy on the brakes and no loops today.
newBrief: These fragile museum pieces need to make it to the new exhibition in one piece. Descend with care, go easy on the brakes, and no, we don't do loops today.

oldBrief: Engineers are expecting this delivery of {cargo_type}. Stick to the block times and get it to the destination. Work has been suspended until you deliver these goods. Don't make them wait.
newBrief: Engineers are waiting on this {cargo_type} and work's stopped until it lands. Stick to the block times and get it there asap.

oldBrief: High-value, luxury vehicles have been secured to the main deck. Make sure the loadmaster checks every strap before the door closes, and no, you can't sit in them.
newBrief: High-value vehicles are secured to the main deck today. Have the loadmaster check every strap before the door closes, and no, you can't sit in them.

oldBrief: A bespoke supercar has been loaded for delivery. Go easy on the controls and confirm the straps are secure before closing up. Do not touch the car. Do not get in the car. Do not breathe on the car.
newBrief: A bespoke supercar is loaded and ready. Go easy on the controls and confirm the straps before you close up. Don't touch the car. Don't get in the car. Don't even breathe on the car.

oldBrief: {cargo_type} and heavy oilfield equipment are bolted to the floor rails. Expect a slower flight; watch the fuel and stay ahead of the power curve on final. We don't want you dropping out of the sky just before you land. Yes, we all remember when that happened.
newBrief: {cargo_type} and heavy oilfield equipment are bolted to the floor rails today. Expect a slower flight, watch your fuel, and stay ahead of the power curve on final.

oldBrief: A retired avionics bay has been requested by a team at your destination airport. Check the tie-downs before you roll and no steep turns on this one.
newBrief: A retired avionics bay is heading back to a restoration team before being transported to a local aviation museum for preservation.

oldBrief: The supermarkets are waiting for this delivery. Keep the temperature steady so nothing spoils. You do want to get paid, don't you?
newBrief: The supermarkets are waiting on this one and nothing back there likes to spoil. Keep the temperature steady the whole way.

oldBrief: This is a delivery of high end consumer electronics straight from the factory. Watch the V-speeds on the takeoff roll and keep the cabin temperature in check.
newBrief: High-end consumer electronics are coming straight from the factory today. Watch your V-speeds on the takeoff roll and keep that cabin temperature in check.

oldBrief: The sort facility is on the clock. Ask for directs if you experience any delays getting in the air.
newBrief: The sort facility's on the clock tonight. Ask for directs the moment you sense any delay getting airborne.

oldBrief: A central-bank transfer of gold bullion needs transporting and there are lots of frowning people dressed in black waiting on the ramp. The ground team will handle loading and offload. Expect an armed team on board for this job.
newBrief: A central-bank gold transfer is waiting on the ramp, along with a lot of serious-looking people dressed in black. The ground crew handles the loading and offload.

oldBrief: The aircraft has been loaded to almost MTOW. Expect a long roll and a lazy climb; double-check the V-speeds before committing and keep the power on.
newBrief: This one's loaded to the roof. Expect close to MTOW on the sheet. Prepare for a long roll and a lazy climb, and double-check your V-speeds before you commit.

oldBrief: This red-eye clears the big sorting hubs. Hit the ATC slots and manage the heavy descent while the sky is quiet.
newBrief: This overnight run needs to get to the big sorting hubs tonight. Hit your ATC slots and manage the heavy descent while the sky stays quiet.

oldBrief: The sort facility is backed up and the hold is stuffed to the roof. Expect a slow rotate and a step-climb if the air is warm tonight.
newBrief: The sort facility's backed up and the hold is stuffed to the roof with impulse buys. Expect a slow rotate and a step-climb if the air's running warm tonight.

oldBrief: The loadmaster is still chaining the oversized plant kit to the main deck. Confirm tie-downs and floor limits before you call for pushback and check fuel before you leave.
newBrief: The loadmaster's still chaining down an oversized plant kit on the main deck. Confirm your tie-downs and floor limits before you call for pushback.

oldBrief: The ground crew are locking down an oversized generator on the deck. Check floor limits, chains and CG before pushback.
newBrief: Ground crew are locking down an oversized generator on the deck. Check your fuel calculations and CG before you start her up.

oldBrief: You have a fragile fan module on board for an AOG recovery. Keep the ride smooth and the hold temp steady.
newBrief: This fragile fan module is headed out for an AOG recovery. Keep the ride smooth and hold the temperature steady the whole way.

oldBrief: You have server racks and data-centre hardware in the hold. Fly smooth, keep cabin temp in spec and do not ask what runs on these machines.
newBrief: Server racks and data-centre hardware are riding in the hold today. Get this cargo to the destination on time.

oldBrief: You are flying the assigned grid so the civic leaflet drop covers the sector evenly. Stay on the planned track.
newBrief: You're flying a pre-assigned route today to ensure leaflet distribution covers the sector evenly.

oldBrief: You are surveying the power and pipeline grid today. Stay within the inspection corridor and keep a sterile cockpit while you are on the line.
newBrief: You're surveying the power and pipeline grid today. Stay inside the inspection corridor and keep a sterile cockpit while you're on the line.

oldBrief: You are low and slow over the fields today. Watch for unmarked power lines and keep the track steady for the survey team.
newBrief: You're low and slow over the fields today. Watch for unmarked power lines and hold that track steady for the survey team.

oldBrief: You are mapping a municipal expansion zone. Hold a steady track along the route so the survey team gets clean readings.
newBrief: You're mapping a municipal expansion zone today. Hold a steady track along the route so the survey team gets clean readings.

oldBrief: You are mapping subsurface anomalies today. Hold constant airspeed and altitude — the magnetometer hates wandering.
newBrief: You're mapping subsurface anomalies today. Hold constant airspeed and altitude, the magnetometer hates it when you wander.

oldBrief: A storm tore through here yesterday. Hold the profile over the damage so the insurance assessors can scan from above.
newBrief: A storm tore through the area yesterday. Hold the profile steady over the damage so the insurance assessors can scan from above.

oldBrief: Researchers want LIDAR passes over suspected ruins below. Hold altitude and track tight across the grid so the survey team gets clean coverage.
newBrief: Researchers want LIDAR passes over some recently discovered ruins today. One of the researchers is called Lara...

oldBrief: You have a photographer on board who needs clean, stable orbits over a few waypoints. Work with the photographer and keep the airframe smooth.
newBrief: You've got a photographer on board who needs clean, stable orbits over a few waypoints today. Work with them and keep the airframe smooth.

oldBrief: Researchers want you over a {sci_fi} on this route. Map it from above and try to ignore the weird static chewing through the radios.
newBrief: Researchers want you over the {sci_fi} so that they can take readings. Try to ignore the weird static chewing through the radios.

oldBrief: You are assisting a visual search for a missing vehicle. Fly low over the last known coordinates and keep your eyes outside for anything that looks like a signal.
newBrief: You're assisting local authorities with a visual search for a missing vehicle today.

oldBrief: The owner of this aircraft says that the GPS is acting up and has asked you to bring it to the nearest service center. Fly carefully and keep your eyes outside if the GPS turns off unexpectedly.
newBrief: The owner says the GPS has been acting up and wants it looked at the nearest service center.

oldBrief: The broker just handed over the keys. This is your new aircraft, congratulations. Fly her home, watch the temperatures and don't push her too hard on your first flight.
newBrief: The broker just handed over the keys to you, this is your aircraft now. Fly her home and don't push her too hard on the first flight.

oldBrief: You have an ordinary staff shuttle today. Nothing fancy — get the passengers there on time.
newBrief: Just an ordinary staff shuttle between industrial sites today, nothing fancy. Get the passengers there on time and butter that landing.

oldBrief: You are conducting a standardization flight in the local pattern. Standard maneuvers and clean radio work.
newBrief: You're conducting a standardization flight in the local pattern today. Standard maneuvers, clean radio work, nothing more.

oldBrief: You have an engineering consultant working paperwork in the back. Find smooth air and keep the inputs gentle.
newBrief: You've got an engineering consultant working through paperwork in the back today. Find smooth air and keep your inputs steady and controlled.

oldBrief: This town relies on your connection. Stick to the schedule — plenty of passengers have onward flights at the hub.
newBrief: This town relies on your connection. Stick to the schedule, plenty of passengers have onward flights waiting for them at the hub.

oldBrief: {name} wants quiet and discretion on this run. Smooth climb, smooth descent and keep the ride soft.
newBrief: {name} wants anonymity and privacy on this charter today. Do not mention your client's name on open frequencies.

oldBrief: You are flying {name} to meet a spiritual guru and the press is watching this flight. Park away from the main building and keep {name} off open channels.
newBrief: {name} is meeting a spiritual guru today. Park away from the main building and keep your client's name off any open channels.

oldBrief: You have a romantic twilight scenic on the books tonight. Smooth RPM, shallow banks and a gentle profile — do not spoil the moment.
newBrief: A romantic twilight scenic flight is on the books tonight. Smooth RPM, shallow banks, a gentle profile all the way, don't go and spoil the moment.

oldBrief: You have a stranded businessman who missed the airline connection and grabbed your last seat. Can you save the day and get him to the hub on time?
newBrief: A stranded businessman missed his airline connection and grabbed your last seat instead. Can you save the day and get him to the hub on time?

oldBrief: You are the only link between these towns today. Plan the fuel, watch the approach winds and butter that landing.
newBrief: You're the only link between these towns today. Plan the fuel, watch the approach winds, and butter that landing for the families waiting.

oldBrief: You have a honeymooning couple on a chartered getaway. Gentle turns, smooth air and a soft landing — match the holiday mood.
newBrief: You've got a honeymooning couple on a chartered getaway today. Gentle turns, smooth air, a soft landing, match the mood they're going for.

oldBrief: You have a regional medical examiner on a time-sensitive call-out. Get to the incident site as fast as you safely can and check the runway before you commit.
newBrief: A regional medical examiner has a time-sensitive call-out today. Get to the incident site as fast as you safely can, and check the runway before you commit.

oldBrief: The deal is done and the keys are handed over. Ferry her to the new home base, watch the temps — unfamiliar airframe today.
newBrief: The deal's done and the keys are on the desk. The owner has asked you to ferry her to her new home base, watch the temperatures, this airframe's still new to flying.

oldBrief: You are gathering meteorological data for the science team. Fly the altitudes and headings they ask for — the readings only count if you nail the profile.
newBrief: You're gathering meteorological data for the science team today. Fly the altitudes and headings they call for, the readings only count if you nail the profile.

oldBrief: You have atmospheric researchers who need to drop sensors ahead of a major pressure shift. Get close enough to observe, but stay clear of the convective cells.
newBrief: Atmospheric researchers need to drop sensors ahead of a major pressure shift today. Get close enough to observe, but stay clear of the convective cells.

oldBrief: You are flying a historic airshow demonstration today. Static display on the ground, then a short aerial routine — check the fluids before you roll.
newBrief: You're flying a historic airshow demonstration today. Static display on the ground, then a short aerial routine, check the fluids before you roll.

oldBrief: You are positioning for a closed-course handicap race. Visual transit to the staging field and keep the airframe clean and trimmed.
newBrief: You're positioning for a closed-course handicap race today. Visual transit to the staging field, keep the airframe clean and trimmed the whole way.

oldBrief: You are chase plane for a historic squadron today. Hold your spacing, stay aware and watch the temps — formation power settings can run hot.
newBrief: You're a chase plane for a historic squadron today. Hold your spacing, stay sharp, and watch the temps, formation power settings can run hot.

oldBrief: You are flying a commemorative low-level transit. Hit time-on-target over the memorial clean and keep it respectful.
newBrief: You're flying a commemorative low-level transit today. Check the paraffin-based oil levels before you leave in case a smoke trail is requested.

oldBrief: You are keeping current in a historic airframe. Local pattern work so you and the aircraft stay approved for the next public display.
newBrief: You're keeping current in this historic airframe today. Local pattern work, nothing more, so you and the aircraft both stay approved for the next public display.

oldBrief: You are delivering a newly restored airframe to the preservation trust. She is irreplaceable — watch the gauges, dodge convective weather and deliver her clean to the museum ramp.
newBrief: This newly restored airframe is irreplaceable and headed to the Aviation museum. Watch the gauges, dodge any convective weather, and deliver her clean to the ramp.

oldBrief: You need to be on the staging grounds before sunset. Cruise power conservative to spare the engine — expect a crowd watching your arrival.
newBrief: You need to be on the staging grounds before sunset today. Keep the cruise power conservative to spare the engine.

oldBrief: You are flying a chartered remembrance flight in memory of those who flew this airframe before you. Keep the maneuvers gentle and the fluids in the green.
newBrief: You're flying a memorial flight in memory of those who flew this airframe before you. Keep the gauges in the green.

oldBrief: You have a classic load for a classic bird. Keep the RPMs synced, mind the cowl flaps and plan your descent early — no speedbrakes on this one.
newBrief: You've got a classic load for a classic bird today. Keep the RPMs synced, mind the cowl flaps, and plan your descent early.

oldBrief: The hold smells terrible, but the payout is good. Easy on the bank angles and grease the landing.
newBrief: The hold smells terrible today, but the payout's good. Easy on the bank angles and grease that landing.

oldBrief: You are moving heavy goods in a vintage airframe today. Watch the engine temps, work the flight engineer panel and expect the controls to feel a bit slow.
newBrief: You're moving heavy goods in a vintage airframe today. Watch the engine temps and expect the controls to feel a touch slower than you're used to.

oldBrief: The warehouse teams are still building the pallets. Hit your departure slot or the whole sort window slips.
newBrief: The warehouse teams are still loading the pallets. Hit your departure slot or the whole sort window slips behind you.

oldBrief: You have a premium overnight cross-country with half the cabin asleep. Keep the pitch smooth and the step-climb easy so the passengers stay that way.
newBrief: Most of your passengers will be sleeping on this premium overnight cross-country.

oldBrief: You have holidaymakers across the country today. Watch the cylinder head temps on the ground and get the cowl flaps sorted early before you pick through any local weather.
newBrief: Holidaymakers are riding cross-country with you today. Watch the cylinder head temps on the ground and get the cowl flaps sorted early.

oldBrief: You have a full load of {industry} executives and engineers for the extraction sites. Have the flight engineer keep cross-feeds tidy so the centre of gravity stays balanced.
newBrief: A full load of {industry} executives and engineers is riding to the extraction site today.

oldBrief: You have sports fans heading to the match. Check carb heat and the de-icing boots before you enter the terminal area.
newBrief: Sports fans are heading to the match with you today. Check the carb heat and the de-icing boots before you enter the terminal area.

oldBrief: You are on an iconic passenger shuttle today. Expect a lazy climb off the runway — mind the power recovery and do not thrash the engines.
newBrief: You're on an iconic passenger shuttle today. Expect a lazy climb off the runway and don't thrash the engines.

oldBrief: You have passengers on a local scenic hop today. Take them around the landmarks on a visual pattern, then set down at the destination and keep clear of the GA traffic.
newBrief: You've got passengers for a local scenic route today. Take them around the landmarks on a visual pattern, then set down at the destination.

oldBrief: You are holding steady for a survey photographer. Work with the photographer and give clean orbits over the waypoints — smooth is everything.
newBrief: You're holding steady for a survey photographer today. Work with them and give clean orbits over the waypoints, smooth is everything here.

oldBrief: You are watching the local transit corridors from above. Hold over the big interchanges so the spotter can call traffic conditions — easy turns, predictable track.
newBrief: You're watching the local transit corridors from above today. Hold over the big interchanges so the spotter can call traffic conditions.

oldBrief: You have a client who wants to skip the gridlock. Direct routing if you can get it and do not hang about.
newBrief: You've got a client who wants to skip the gridlock. Grab direct routing if you can get it, and don't hang about.

oldBrief: You are searching for a stranded group of travellers. Work patterns over the last known coordinates and be ready to hoist if you cannot put down.
newBrief: You're searching for a stranded group of travellers today. Work your patterns over the last known coordinates and be ready to hoist.

oldBrief: You are providing aerial overwatch for ground units. Talk to the ground team, hold a safe height over the target area and stay predictable.
newBrief: You're providing aerial overwatch for ground units today. Talk to the ground team, hold a safe height over the target area, and keep your eyes out of the cockpit.

oldBrief: You are mapping a new property development. Fly precise tracks across the survey grid so the cameras get clean, overlapping coverage.
newBrief: You're mapping a new property development today. Fly precise tracks across the survey grid so the cameras get clean, overlapping coverage.

oldBrief: You are positioning industrial equipment with a precision hover. Watch torque and engine limits the whole time you are hanging there.
newBrief: You're positioning industrial equipment with a precision hover today. Watch your torque and engine limits the whole time and watch out for FOD.

oldBrief: You are locating tagged animal populations for the biologists. Keep visual contact while the telemetry is logged and do not spook the wildlife if you can help it.
newBrief: You're locating tagged animal populations for the biologists today. Keep visual contact while the telemetry data is saved.

oldBrief: You have an executive hop from the FBO to the helipad. Smooth transition, soft set-down and no drama.
newBrief: You've got an executive hop from the FBO to the helipad today. Smooth transition, soft set-down, no drama.

oldBrief: You are covering a civic event live from the air. Set up a loiter clear of other traffic and keep your movements predictable for the camera operator.
newBrief: You're covering a civic event live from the air today. Set up a hover clear of other traffic and keep your movements predictable for the camera operator.

oldBrief: You are capturing dynamic tracking shots today. Work with the ground director, match the subject's pace and keep the follow smooth with no sudden inputs.
newBrief: You're capturing dynamic tracking shots today. Work with the ground director, match the subject's pace, and keep your flying smooth with no sudden inputs.

oldBrief: You have external load work moving heavy pipe segments into rugged terrain. Watch torque and rotor RPM while you ease the segments into place.
newBrief: You've got external load work today. Remember to use the specialized rigging techniques you were taught, to avoid dangerous load spinning.

oldBrief: You are cleaning high-tension lines today. Fly low and slow so the boom operator can hit the insulators. Mind the wind — you do not want to drift into the wires.
newBrief: You're cleaning high-tension lines using high-pressure jets of demineralized water while the power grid remains fully active.

oldBrief: You have highly sensitive legal tenders on board and the case is handcuffed to the courier. Fly straight and be ready for an engine-running offload the moment you arrive.
newBrief: You've got highly sensitive documents on board and the package is handcuffed to the courier.

oldBrief: Hikers found a smooth, heavy metal pillar in a slot canyon. Ground crews say the air goes cold near it and your compass will not settle.
newBrief: A group of hikers found an impossibly smooth and heavy metal pillar out in a slot canyon. Ground crews say the air goes cold near it and their hair stands on end.

oldBrief: You have a heavy tactical load today. Double-check the CG on the loadsheet before you start the engines.
newBrief: Heavy tactical load transport today. Verify the CG on the loadsheet before engine start and double check vehicles are secured before takeoff.

oldBrief: The depot needs this kit for assembly the moment you land. Stick to the filed plan and hit the block.
newBrief: Depot needs this kit for assembly on arrival. Stick to the filed plan. Hit the block.

oldBrief: You have sealed manifests and no questions on this run. Head straight for the remote ramp when you arrive.
newBrief: Sealed manifests today. No questions asked. Head straight for the remote ramp on arrival.

oldBrief: You have a priority load on board. Get it there on time or the maintenance schedule slips.
newBrief: Priority load on board. Get it there on time. Miss the window and the maintenance schedule slips.

oldBrief: Maintenance are standing by for this hardware. Do not waste a minute on the way in.
newBrief: Maintenance is standing by for this hardware. Don't waste a minute getting it in.

oldBrief: You have palletized military stores going on the main deck. Check tie-down tension and CG before you start engines.
newBrief: Palletized military stores on the main deck. Check tie-down tension and CG before engine start.

oldBrief: You have humanitarian pallets bound for a forward distribution point. Keep the schedule and make sure the offload teams are ready when you land.
newBrief: Humanitarian pallets bound for a forward distribution point. Keep the schedule. Confirm offload teams will be waiting on your arrival.

oldBrief: You are deploying a specialized ground team into the LZ. Use the terrain on the way in, stabilize the hover and get the team out clean.
newBrief: Deploying a specialized ground team into the LZ. Use the terrain on the approach. Stabilize the hover.

oldBrief: We have reports of suspicious movement along the vector. Hold corridor track, log contacts and watch loiter fuel. Do not engage.
newBrief: Reports of suspicious movement along the vector. Hold corridor track. Log contacts. Watch loiter fuel. Do not engage.

oldBrief: You have visiting dignitaries on board who want clear photos of the base from a safe standoff. Soft ride and predictable banks.
newBrief: Visiting dignitaries want clear photos of the base from a safe standoff. Soft ride. Predictable banks.

oldBrief: You are outbound to the training grid for low-altitude hover work. Keep your eyes peeled for the training beacons.
newBrief: Outbound to the training grid for low-altitude hover work. Watch for the training beacons.

oldBrief: You have field rations and spare radio batteries in the back. Ease into the LZ and watch for wind shear off the terrain.
newBrief: Field rations and spare radio batteries in the back. Ease into the LZ. Watch for wind shear off the terrain.

oldBrief: You have regional commanders on board for a joint briefing. Comfortable transit, direct routing and no sightseeing — security wants you there with no detours.
newBrief: Regional commanders are on board for a joint briefing. Fly a comfortable transit, direct routing. No detours, security's orders.

oldBrief: You have secure flight data recorders from a defense contractor on board. Standard OPSEC — keep it quiet and stick to the plan.
newBrief: Secure flight data recorders from a defense contractor are being loaded. Standard OPSEC. Keep quiet. Stick to the plan.

oldBrief: You have unmarked secure containers on the flight plan. Talk normally on the radio, but go straight to destination.
newBrief: Unmarked secure containers on the flight plan. No questions. Go straight to destination.

oldBrief: You have a standard military charter with contracted defense personnel on board. Hit the schedule and fly it like any heavy jet sector.
newBrief: Standard military charter with contracted defense personnel aboard. Fly it like any heavy jet sector and bring these troops to their new base.

oldBrief: You are on a peacetime repositioning to a strategic staging airfield. Sterile cockpit and work with military ATC for your arrival window.
newBrief: Peacetime repositioning to a strategic staging airfield. Sterile cockpit. Work with military ATC for your arrival window.

oldBrief: You are executing a peacetime navigation exercise. Nail the fuel plan and the waypoint timings — fly the exercise by the numbers.
newBrief: Nail the fuel plan and waypoint timings. Fly it by the numbers. Refuelling is available en route if required.

oldBrief: You have a low-profile transit with staff personnel under escort. Direct routing, assigned levels and no deviations from the flightplan.
newBrief: Low-profile transit of key defense personnel under UAV escort. Direct routing, assigned levels. No deviations from the flight plan.

oldBrief: You have priority diplomatic communications on board. Maintain chain of custody and do not leave the filed flightpath.
newBrief: Priority diplomatic communications on board. Maintain chain of custody. Stay on the filed flight path.

oldBrief: Captain, this flight officially does not exist. Ignore any knocking from the hold and do not log the sector.
newBrief: Captain, this flight officially does not exist. Ignore any knocking from the hold and do not go back there to check. Do not log this flight.

oldBrief: You are providing high-speed SAR support along the route. Scan for beacons or visual distress, pass coordinates to the extraction teams and hold your search profile.
newBrief: High-speed SAR support along the route. Scan for beacons or visual distress. Pass coordinates to the extraction teams. Hold your search profile.

oldBrief: You are patrolling the designated vector for surface anomalies. Keep eyes on the surface and call any unregistered traffic up to sector command.
newBrief: Patrolling the designated vector for surface anomalies. Eyes on the surface. Call any unregistered traffic up to sector command.

oldBrief: You are holding steady over the sector as a UHF/VHF relay for ground exercises. Watch your fuel and monitor your instruments and oxygen.
newBrief: Holding steady over the sector as a UHF/VHF relay for ground exercises. Watch your fuel. Monitor instruments and oxygen.

oldBrief: You are gathering passive telemetry data today. Fly the filed route exactly so the onboard equipment can triangulate regional signal traffic.
newBrief: Gathering passive telemetry data. Fly the filed route exactly. Onboard equipment needs precision to triangulate regional signal traffic accurately.

oldBrief: You are providing a target profile for ground early warning systems. Hold the altitude and airspeed in your flightplan so the stations can calibrate their radar returns.
newBrief: Providing a target profile for ground-based early warning systems. Hold altitude and airspeed exactly as filed. This data is needed to calibrate radar returns.

oldBrief: You are intercepting unidentified radar contacts. Keep speed up and watch the tactical displays for vectored intercepts.
newBrief: Intercepting unidentified radar contacts. Keep your speed up. Watch the tactical displays for vectored intercepts. This might be E.T.

oldBrief: You are on a cooperative cross-service nav exercise. Match profiles with the allied assets — timing has to be spot-on for the rendezvous.
newBrief: Cooperative cross-service navigation exercise. Match profiles with the allied assets. Timing has to be spot-on for the rendezvous.

oldBrief: Ground stations need a clean target for tracking telemetry. Keep the airframe smooth — the pods hate vibration.
newBrief: Ground stations need a clean target for tracking telemetry. Keep the airframe stable. These new pods hate vibration.

oldBrief: You are re-validating primary approach vectors today. Non-precision approach practice — log the navaids properly and fly it by the book.
newBrief: Re-validating primary approach vectors. Non-precision approach practice. Log the navaids properly. Fly by the book.

oldBrief: You are on a ferry flight for off-cycle maintenance. Watch your temps and keep the engines happy.
newBrief: Ferry flight for off-cycle maintenance. Watch your temps. Keep the engines cool.

oldBrief: You are on a two-ship proficiency transit. Keep wingman separation inside the limits through climb and cruise — no surprises.
newBrief: Two-ship proficiency transit. Do not try to recreate that scene from Top Gun again, you have your orders.

oldBrief: You are conducting a handling and proficiency check. Fly the filed route with sharp energy management and respect the floor altitudes in the simulated combat phase.
newBrief: Handling and proficiency check. Fight through the G's and try not to black out.

oldBrief: You are executing a terrain-masking profile today. Terrain-following or strict visual low-level — hold 250 feet AGL through the corridor and watch for birds.
newBrief: High-speed terrain-masking profile. Hold 250 feet AGL through the corridor. Watch for birds and smile for the cameras.

oldBrief: You have been instructed to be on the staging grounds before sunset. Cruise power to spare the engines — expect a crowd watching your arrival.
newBrief: You've been instructed to arrive before 7am. This is a busy airfield, so watch out for slow civilian flights on arrival.

oldBrief: You are conducting aerial refuelling approach practice. Fly the assigned route and hold airspeed and altitude per your flightplan the whole way.
newBrief: Aerial refuelling approach practice, same drill as always. Hold airspeed and altitude as briefed, and try not to break another refuelling nozzle.

oldBrief: You are flying departure to destination on the assigned recon route. Hold altitude and airspeed so the sensors collect continuous imagery along the corridor.
newBrief: Fly departure to destination on the assigned recon route. Hold altitude and airspeed. Sensors need continuous imagery along the corridor.

oldBrief: You are mapping the assigned transit corridor today. Fly direct, hold a steady track and altitude and let the mapping systems build a clean picture.
newBrief: Mapping the assigned transit corridor. Fly direct. Hold a steady track and altitude. Let the mapping systems build a clean picture.

oldBrief: You are photographing designated areas along the route. Match the briefed headings and timings so analysts can sync the imagery to the mission clock.
newBrief: Your mission is to photograph designated areas along the route. Analysts need the imagery synced with the waypoints in your flight plan, no deviations.

oldBrief: You are on a two-ship formation transit, departure to destination. Keep wingman spacing inside limits through the climb and cruise.
newBrief: Two-ship formation transit, from departure to destination. Keep wingman spacing inside limits through the climb and cruise.

oldBrief: You are conducting aerial refuelling approach practice. Hold airspeed and altitude as briefed and do not break another refuelling nozzle.
newBrief: Aerial refuelling approach practice, same drill as always. Hold airspeed and altitude as briefed, and try not to break another refuelling nozzle.

oldBrief: Stay in the local area above {dep_field}. Practice thermalling, position reports and clean circuit entries. Under developing cumulus, core the strongest lift. Recover to the glider strip when your block time expires.
newBrief: Stay in the local area above {dep_field} today. Feel for lift and bank smoothly into the rising air. Return to the airfield if the weather conditions worsen.

oldBrief: You are working whatever lift the day offers between {dep_field} and {dest_field}. Use thermals under growing Cu, slope lift or cloud streets where you can. Stay clear of lee turbulence and do not press into sink without a landing option.
newBrief: Use rising air currents to gain altitude between {dep_field} and {dest_field}. Ride thermals wherever you find them. Stay clear of lee-side turbulence and scan for alternative landing options.

oldBrief: You have a student aboard for handling and lookout practice. Demonstrate energy management and circuit work, and talk through how you read the sky as you fly. Keep the ride smooth and verbalize every decision.
newBrief: A student's aboard from {dep_field} for handling and lookout practice today. Talk through how you're reading the sky as you go.

oldBrief: The club needs this glider repositioned from {dep_field} to {dest_field}. Climb to a safe altitude, shut down to soar when you can and keep enough battery or fuel for a go-around reserve at destination.
newBrief: The club needs this glider repositioned from {dep_field} to {dest_field}. Climb to a safe altitude, shut down and soar whenever you can.

oldBrief: You are flying a practice speed task from {dep_field} to {dest_field}. Work your height band, plan turns before weak lift and use cloud streets to cover ground. Progress by soaring technique, not minimum time under engine power.
newBrief: A practice speed task from {dep_field} to {dest_field} today. Work your height band, plan the turns before you hit weak lift, and lean on cloud streets to cover distance.
